source.rawText: HomeStudy With UsInformation for International StudentsScholarships The Keates-Lee Educational Trust Bursary The Keates-Lee Educational Trust Bursary The Keates-Lee Educational Trust Bursary is a £4,000 1st year scholarship available to high-achieving undergraduate students from African nations. This scholarship will be awarded to 2 successful candidates each September intake. EligibilityStudents must be applying for a 3-year or 4-year undergraduate programme in one of the following subject areas: Accounting and Finance Agriculture Biosciences Business & Management Ecological Sciences Economics Engineering Geography, Earth & Environmental Science Law Political & International Relations Veterinary Studies Applicants must meet one of the following criteria: Are permanently resident in an African nation. Are refugees, domiciled in the UK, who have been forcibly displaced due to recent or ongoing conflict; persecution; or humanitarian crises. Students must be international-fee payers. Students must be self-funding and not in receipt of any external scholarships. Students should meet the University’s usual entry requirements, including completion of high school within 2 years of the start date at Aberystwyth University. Students must be high-performing in their high school grades, demonstrating they have achieved or are on track to achieve one of the following, or equivalent, as deemed by the scholarship awards committee: A-level 3 x B Grades and above IB score of 32 and above US Diploma GPA of 3.2 or above Minimum 3 x A1 Grades at WAEC/NECO/WASSCE Overall A in KCSE Minimum 3 x scores of 7 in NSC Moroccan Bac. 16/20 Algerian Bac. 16/20 UACE 3 x B Grades and above September 2026 Timeline February 27th 12:00 GMT: Application Deadline March 27th: Successful, reserve, and unsuccessful candidates will be notified of the outcome of their application. The scholarship offers 2 routes of application, each with different eligibility criteria. source.rawText: Check here regularly for our most up-to-date list of International Foundation Pathway scholarships. Reading Excellence ScholarshipWe offer a number of scholarships worth £5,000 for students starting an International Foundation Programme (IFP) or International Foundation Year (IFY) in 2026/27. If you hold an offer for an IFP or IFY, you may be eligible to apply for this scholarship. Apply now on Me@Reading applicant portal. Deadlines Round one: 19 May 2026 (for September 2026 entry) Round two: 14 July 2026 (for September 2026 entry) Round three: 16 November (for January 2027 entry) Before applying for the Reading Excellence Scholarship IFP/IFY, please read our Guidance on Completing the Scholarship Application Form. By submitting an application form, you are agreeing to the terms and conditions. Key information To apply for funding, you must have received an offer to join an IFP or IFY course in the academic year 2026/27. The scholarship application form will be made available to eligible students via the Me@Reading applicant portal. You will be able to access it until the closing date. The scholarship will take the form of a tuition fee reduction of £5,000 for the IFP/IFY year of study. The University must classify you as an international student for fee purposes. Scholarships are awarded primarily based on previous academic accomplishment. Undergraduate scholarshipsWhen you progress to an undergraduate degree at the University of Reading, you may be eligible for some of our undergraduate scholarships and discounts. This includes our University of Reading Global Sustainability Leaders Scholarship, designed to create the sustainability leaders of tomorrow. This new and exciting undergraduate scholarship scheme aims to create a community of future global sustainability leaders. source.rawText: Home Your Roehampton life Sports and Activities Sport Roehampton Sport Scholarship Sport Scholarship If you excel in sport, we can provide extensive financial and mentoring support, so you can study your degree whilst competing at national or international standard in your chosen activity. We offer scholarships ranging from £500 to £1,500 per year, depending on your level of performance. This scholarship can be combined with additional support to help you achieve your potential in both sporting performance and in your degree. This includes mentoring, access to the University of Roehampton gym and academic support. Current and potential 2024 applicants are invited to apply now for the Roehampton University Scholarship for Sporting Excellence programme. The scholarships are available to students who will be studying on any Roehampton course, at any level, undergraduate or postgraduate. In your application you need to demonstrate your commitment to your chosen sport and your ability to combine academic progression with sporting excellence. Your application will be assessed by a panel, chaired by the Sport Roehampton Manager. Deadline for Scholarships applications for students starting in January: 16 January 2024 Deadline for Scholarships applications for students starting in September: 15 August 2024 Who should apply? Talented sportswomen and sportsmen who have achieved representative honours at a national or regional level, or have the potential to achieve this level of performance whilst studying at Roehampton. Applications are welcome from any sporting background, but particularly those which have team and individual national student competitions. For a list of such sports, see www.bucs.org.uk. If you are unsure as to whether this is you, please contact James Ayres, Sport Roehampton Manager for an informal discussion. Applications for 2026 entry are now closed. To be considered for our Vice-Chancellor’s Scholarship Exam you will need to sit, and pass, two exam papers in subjects of your choice* with the exams being held at your school/college, or an alternative agreed invigilation centre. Students who successfully complete the exams will be awarded one of the following, based on their performance: Vice Chancellor's Scholarship: For the top 20% of all international students who pass the exams in that academic year. Successful students will receive a tuition-fee discount of £3,000 per year for every year of their undergraduate studies (maximum of £9,000). If students successfully pass the exams, they may also be given an unconditional offer to study with us. Vice Chancellor’s Merit Award: For the remaining 80% of all international students who pass the exams in that academic year. Successful students will receive a tuition-fee discount of £3,000 in the first year only, and £2,00 for each subsequent year. If students successfully pass the exams, they may also be given an unconditional offer to study with us. *Please ensure that you select exam papers which are acceptable to the Department(s) you have applied to study at. It is your responsibility to ensure you have selected appropriate subjects. Failure to do so may result in your scholarship application being rejected. Please note that Veterinary Science, Veterinary Nursing and Nursing applicants are not eligible to sit the exams. source.rawText: HomeStudy With UsInformation for International StudentsScholarships International Family AwardInternational Family AwardAberystwyth University has a strong connection with its current students and alumni, and often sees generations of families following in the footsteps of their relatives to complete their degrees with us. For this reason, we have developed the International Family Award. If you are a new, international student (paying international tuition fees) and one of your family relatives studied, or is studying, a degree at Aberystwyth University, you may be eligible for the International Family Award – giving you a £1,000 reduction in tuition fees for every year of your studies.How to Apply Submit your application directly: You must first submit your application for your chosen degree directly to Aberystwyth University, without using the services of an Education Agent. If you need support making your application, please get in touch with the international recruitment team international@aber.ac.uk; Accept your offer: Once you have received a conditional or unconditional offer of a place you must accept the offer by returning your ‘Offer Reply Form’, or by selecting Aberystwyth as your Firm choice through UCAS; Submit your Award application: Once you have accepted your offer, you can apply for the International Family Award by completing this Application Form by September 1st, with details of your relative who studies/studied at Aberystwyth. Terms and Conditions To be eligible for the International Family Award, you must submit your application to study directly to the University, without using the services of an education agent. source.rawText: Personal circumstances scholarships If your household income is less than £42,875 a year, you may be eligible to apply for a means-tested undergraduate scholarship which offers funding and support. The deadline for scholarship applications for 2026 entry has now passed, and no further applications can be accepted. If you have applied for a scholarship for 2026 entry, you should hear from us by August 2026. Applications for 2027 entry will open in March 2027. Information relating to scholarships changes from time to time. While the University endeavours to keep this information as up to date as possible, it cannot be held liable for any inaccuracies. If you defer entry for a year, you will generally need to apply for financial support applicable to your year of entry. Find out about the scholarships The funding you receive Worth £3,000 a year for three years (paid in cash instalments), our UK undergraduate means-tested scholarships are of higher value than the University’s funding package Leeds Bursary (funding which is automatically awarded based on a student’s household income level). The scholarships do not have to be paid back and are in addition to the financial support you can receive from the government (such as the tuition fee loan or maintenance loan). Students who are able to evidence that they are care experienced and/or estranged from their parents during the application process will be eligible for an additional £2,000 annually. The support you receive Alongside the funding, you'll have access to one-to-one support and advice sessions, group workshops, mentoring opportunities, social events and monthly newsletters updating you on relevant activity on and off campus through the Plus Programme. There are a limited number of scholarships available. We will award the UK undergraduate means-tested scholarships to selected UK students from low income households who also meet the eligibility criteria and are entering Leeds as full-time, level one undergraduates

These will be part-funded scholarships and at least three will be awarded to female applicants to support our Women in STEM agenda. Scholarship details The University of Salford's MSc Data Science programme is ideal for mathematics, computing or science graduates, or experienced professionals, eager to join the data storytelling revolution. MSc Data Science requires students to take a live project as the final part of the degree. The live projects will be supplied by EATL Innovation Hub and will be focused on solving a problem that has an impact on the development of Bangladesh. This is a key impact of this initiative – our students will be working on a project that relates to global development including aligning to UN Sustainable Development Goals. There are four scholarships available for January 2026 intake. Applicants must be of Bangladesh nationality. At least two scholarships will be awarded to female applicants to support our Women in STEM agenda. The scholarship is awarded as a tuition fee reduction of £7,100. Award winners will pay a reduced tuition fee of £12,000 (instead of the full tuition fee of £19,100) for September 2025 intake. This is not a full scholarship and award winners must behave funds available for the remaining tuition fee and living costs associated with studying at the University of Salford in the UK. How to apply This is a selective scholarship. You must first complete the Salford-EATL scholarship application on our dedicated Salford/EATL webpage. NCUK delivers pathway programmes that lead to degrees at member universities. NCUK foundation and graduate pathway programmes are taught in its accredited centres around the world. Since 1987, hundreds of students have progressed onto the University of Salford after completing NCUK programmes and are now working successfully around the world. To support students who progress from NCUK, we offer a number of high value scholarships to outstanding applicants for undergraduate or master's programmes. Scholarship details The NCUK Undergraduate Excellence Scholarship is worth £5,000. The NCUK Undergraduate Excellence Scholarship (progression from IY1) is worth £3,000. The NCUK Postgraduate Excellence Scholarship (progression from PMP) is worth £3,000. The NCUK Salford Undergraduate Excellence Scholarship is open to applicants who have an offer for an undergraduate programme and have achieved 128 UCAS points (A level grades ABB grades or equivalent) and a minimum EAP C in the NCUK International Foundation Year. The NCUK Salford Undergraduate Excellence Scholarship (progression from IY1) is open to applicants who have studied the NCUK International Year One and have an offer for an undergraduate programme. Scholarship details The Chevening scholarship is worth 100% of the tuition fee, a monthly stipend and airfares. source.rawText: ‹ Funding Home Study at Northumbria Support for Students Financial support Funding Funding for International Students Funding for International Students At Northumbria, we're proud to welcome talented students from around the world. We understand that studying in the UK is a significant financial commitment, and are here to support you with a range of fee discounts, scholarships, and practical financial guidance to help you succeed. Tuition and Funding Northumbria offers a range of scholarships and discounts for international students. For more information, please visit our International Scholarships page. As an international student, you are not eligible for UK student loans, so it’s essential to plan how you will fund your studies and living costs before you arrive. Support for EU/EEA Students If you're an EU or EEA national planning to study in the UK, your access to student funding will depend on your immigration status. If you arrived in the UK after 31 December 2020, you are generally not eligible for Student Finance England funding unless you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (EUSS). If you do have settled or pre-settled status, you may be eligible for tuition fee loans, and in some cases, full support including maintenance funding - especially if you are classed as a migrant worker or are the family member of one. If you do not have settled status, you will need to apply for a Student visa to study in the UK. Irish citizens continue to benefit from free movement and may qualify for student funding depending on residency and work history. Useful links: GOV.UK - UK Visa Requirements GOV.UK - Student Finance for EU Nationals Bringing Dependants If you will be bringing dependants, especially dependant children, with you whilst you study in the UK, you will need to consider additional requirements, including the availability of childcare or schools in the area you plan to live. scholarships.name: Sir Terence Etherton Scholarship

source.rawText: You are here: Birkbeck, University of London Student services Financial support Sir Terence Etherton Scholarship Sir Terence Etherton Scholarship Award overviewLevel: Undergraduate, postgraduateMode of study: Full-time, part-timeTuition fee status: HomeValue: £3,500Number of awards: Up to twoDeadline: 30 September 2026A scholarship of £3,500 is offered for students of law in their final year of an LLB or LLMQLD course. We are able to offer this scholarship due to the generosity of The Right Hon. Sir Terence Etherton, Baron Etherton, who left a substantial legacy to Birkbeck, University of London to support students of the Birkbeck Law School.Sir Terence was elected a Fellow of Birkbeck in 2019, following a period as a Visiting Professor of Law and a Patron of the Birkbeck Law Review. He had a distinguished career in the law culminating in serving as Chancellor of the High Court from 2013 to 2016, and as the Master of the Rolls and Head of Civil Justice from 2016 to 2021. You can read more about Sir Terence’s life in his obituary.EligibilityApplicants must be on an LLB or LLMQLD course based at our Bloomsbury campus (including courses delivered online), and be expecting to progress onto the final year of study in the 2026/27 academic year.Applicants must have a household income below £42,875.This scholarship is competitive and will be awarded to the students who are best able to demonstrate both academic excellence and the impact receiving this scholarship would make on their studies.ValueThe scholarship value is £3,500 and will be paid to the student to assist with their study and living costs.DeadlineApplications for this scholarship must be received by 30 September 2026.How to applyPlease complete the online application form.Birkbeck reserves the right to withdraw or amend a scholarship without prior notification. Scholarships are offered subject to funding and availability.

Scholarships are essential for ensuring we can bring the best and brightest students to SOAS in an increasingly competitive market and regardless of their financial situation. Support for students is more important now than ever before. Using surpluses in recent years, SOAS has invested significantly in our endowment which has grown to £10m, enabling us to extend more financial support to our students. This, along with support from our alumni and supporter communities, has meant we have awarded more than 450 scholarships in the last decade. Supporting scholarships Scholarship FundUnrestricted gifts to the scholarship fund give us the freedom to respond to the priorities of our students. These unrestricted gifts help open the doors of SOAS to exceptional students from around the world. Scholarships are awarded to individuals who are not only academically outstanding, but who also bring unique perspectives, lived experience, and a passion for creating positive change. Some awards support students from underrepresented regions or communities; others help attract future leaders in their fields. Your success is our success – we’re #BUProud that 89% of our graduates are in work or further study (HESA Graduate outcomes 2022/23). Our TEF (Teaching Excellence Framework) Silver rating recognises the student experience and student outcomes are typically of very high quality. We recognise the importance of work placements to put your skills into practice in the real world, build your network and grow your confidence. source.rawText: AECC School of Chiropractic Celebrates International Research Excellence with Best Poster Award Win Back AECC School of Chiropractic - 21 May 2026 - 2 minute read. Health Sciences University is proud to celebrate the outstanding achievement of Erdi Shaba, PhD student and Chiropractic Lecturer within the AECC School of Chiropractic, who has been awarded the Best Poster Award at the prestigious European Chiropractors’ Union (ECU) Conference in Zurich. Erdi’s winning research, entitled “What Works, For Whom, In What Circumstance And How: A Realist Synthesis Of Health Promotion In Chiropractic Care”, impressed an international panel of experts and reflects the University’s continuing commitment to impactful, evidence-based research in musculoskeletal (MSK) health. This recognition highlights both the strength of AECC’s research culture and the growing contribution of chiropractic scholarship to global healthcare conversations. Erdi’s work focuses on a sophisticated and evolving methodological approach, realist synthesis, that offers nuanced insight into how health promotion strategies function across different patient populations and contexts. A Commitment to Research Excellence Daniel Moore, Head of AECC School of Chiropractic, praised the achievement: “Having our AECC School of Chiropractic staff and students engaged in research at an international level, is part of our commitment to research and innovation at the highest levels. This award is testament to Erdi’s commitment, and that of his supervisory team. The School and University more broadly are extremely proud of that commitment.” Dr Alister du Rose also reflected on the significance of the recognition and the quality of Erdi’s presentation: “It was so pleasing to see Erdi deliver his poster presentation to some of the world’s leading MSK healthcare experts, his mastery of what is a relatively unknown and complex methodology ‘a realist review’ was clear to the panel, and his hard work so far has clearly paid off

scholarships.name: Managing Your Money While Studying

source.rawText: Managing your money while studying If you’re moving to York for your studies, getting to grips with your spending will help you plan ahead. We know thinking about money can feel daunting, but support is always close by. If you have any concerns about managing your money, let us know – we'd love to show you what's possible. 💡 Did you know? WhatUni's Student Budget Calculator is a good start towards working out how much you'll spend when living independently as a student. In the meantime, take a peek at some of our students' top tips… Rent 🏡 Outside of tuition fees, living in rented accommodation will likely be your biggest expense. Most York students choose Uni-managed accommodation in their first year. We have plenty of options for different budgets, so prices will vary with your room choice – size, location, bathroom type, and so on. 💎 Tip: All our accommodation includes bills (electricity, water, high-speed internet, etc) and other protections (contents insurance, 24/7 security, etc). It goes a long way to simplifying your experience as a first-time budgeter. Explore rooms and prices Usually, students look for private accommodation from their second year of study onwards. Again, York has options to suit, and we’re always on-hand to help you through the process. 💎 Tip: You’ll likely be eligible to pay less or no council tax as a student here. Make sure you talk to City of York Council when you’re moving in to avoid paying what you don’t need. Explore private accommodation VLOG Food 🍲 Like your rent, how much you spend on food will vary a good deal based on where you shop and what you eat. York is home to all major supermarkets (with two stores on campus), and all kinds of cafes, bars and restaurants, so you’re well covered for choice. 💎 Tip: Lots of our accommodation options are catered, which means you’ll get ten meals a week included in your room price. 💎 Tip: Our Meals in Advance Deal gives all students the chance to get in on the action, too. source.rawText: Ernest Edward Scholarship 2026 Aston University Scholarship Aston University is delighted to offer up to four sanctuary scholarships for students who are seeking refuge in the UK. These scholarships benefit asylum seekers or those who have been granted a form of limited permission to stay in the UK, following an unsuccessful asylum application, and who are therefore prevented from accessing student finance. These sanctuary scholarships are known as The Ernest Edward Scholarships in memory of the generous donor’s grandfather, Ernest Edward Crummack, who left school aged 12 to work in a coal mine. 100 years on, so many young people and especially young refugees still find themselves deprived of the opportunity to grow and fulfil their potential. Ernest Edward Scholars receive a full tuition fee waiver, support with accommodation and living costs, and additional non-cash support. The scholarship is worth up to £20,000 for postgraduate taught courses and up to £45,000 for undergraduate courses over the duration of the programme. The actual amount awarded may vary, as support is calculated according to individual need and determined on a case by case basis. Scholars also have access to tailored support, including language support where needed, Sports Aston membership, professional mentoring, and support from Aston’s Students’ Union. Summary of eligibility criteria Ernest Edward Scholarship not for you? Aston University offers many other undergraduate and postgraduate for home and international students. Ernest Edward Scholarships 2026 Course: You must have applied to study a course at Aston University. Most three-year undergraduate and one-year postgraduate courses are eligible but certain courses such as medicine and nursing are not eligible. They are paid directly to the university by the Student Loans Company, so, once your loan has been approved, you won’t have to worry about remembering to pay your fees. You need to apply to your relevant funding body for your Tuition Fee Loan, by filling in an online application. You don’t need to have been accepted on a course or made a firm decision about where you’d like to study when you apply for funding - you can use the details of the course you’re most likely to attend initially and can amend this at a later date if you need to. source.rawText: HomeStudyInternationalInternational fees and fundingHow to pay your deposit – for applicants with overseas fee status How to pay your deposit – for applicants with overseas fee status This page provides essential information about deposit payment and fee payments once you have received and accepted your offer. To secure your place on the course, both international undergraduate and postgraduate students are required to pay a deposit. It is essential that you pay your deposit by the deadline specified in your offer letter. Not paying the deposit on time will result in a delay to your CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies), which is necessary for your Student visa application. Delayed payment can also impact your ability to enrol in the course for that intake, as UKVI visa processing times can vary depending on factors such as application volumes and individual circumstances. To ensure a smooth process and avoid any disruptions to your enrolment, we strongly recommend making the deposit payment promptly. Find information on: How do I pay my deposit? source.rawText: Scholarship information The Cambridge Australia Scholarships are available to Masters and PhD applicants from Australia in all subjects. They are tenable at any College of the University of Cambridge. Offered in partnership with Cambridge Australia Scholarships. Value Masters: Part-cost scholarship. PhD: Full-cost scholarship, covering: University tuition fee (International rate). Annual maintenance (sufficient for a single person). Contribution towards student Immigration Health Surcharge. Contribution towards travel. How to apply No separate application is required for this scholarship, only the application for admission to the University of Cambridge, which must be submitted by the funding deadline specific to your course. Please refer to the Postgraduate Course Directory. For more information please visit our Postgraduate applicants page. Funding Partner: View Partner Profile Cambridge Australia Scholarships Cambridge Australia Scholarships (CAS) is a not-for-profit organisation that provides scholarships for outstanding Australian graduates to undertake Masters and PhD degrees at the University of Cambridge. Since its establishment in the 1980s (as the Cambridge Australia Trust), over 350 scholarships have been awarded in partnership with the Cambridge Trust under a variety of schemes, many of them named after donors or eminent Australian alumni. CAS relies on the generosity of its donors, and all of its scholarships are funded by private philanthropic gifts. In recognition of its generosity in funding Australian students at Cambridge, in 2011 CAS was inducted into the University’s Guild of Benefactors. Cambridge Australia Scholarships are funded jointly by CAS and the Cambridge Trust, and are available to Australian applicants at Masters and PhD level.

source.rawText: Bath professor named Honorary Fellow of the Chinese Chemical Society Professor Tony James has been recognised for his world-leading research by the Chinese Chemical Society (2025). Press release Published on Monday 8 June 2026 Last updated on Tuesday 9 June 2026 View more announcements in Communications Professor Tony James Professor Tony James, from the University of Bath’s Department of Chemistry and Institute of Sustainability and Climate Change, has been named Honorary Fellow of the Chinese Chemical Society (2025), awarded to outstanding, internationally renowned scientists who have contributed to the exchange between the Chinese Chemical Society and international scientists. To date, 114 world-leading scientists have been awarded honorary members of the Chinese Chemical Society, with only a handful of these coming from the UK. Professor James is a fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry, European Academy of Sciences and is an internationally renowned expert in supramolecular chemistry and chemical sensing. The Honorary Fellowship recognises his significant contributions in fluorescence chemical sensing, molecular identification, and diagnostic chemistry, especially in the design of molecular systems related to glucose fluorescence sensing and continuous glucose monitoring, with broad international influence. He has maintained long-term cooperative relationships with many Chinese universities and research institutions, conducting joint research and cultivating talent in molecular sensing, fluorescence imaging, and diagnostic and therapeutic fields. He also actively participates in international academic exchanges and collaborations, making positive contributions to the development of China's supramolecular chemistry and chemical sensing fields, and enhancing the international influence of related fields. source.rawText: Equivalent and lower qualification fee If you are a Home student who has already completed a previous undergraduate programme of study, you will be classed as an Equivalent or Lower Qualification (ELQ) student. The information on this page does not apply to you if you are:classified as Overseas for fee purposesundertaking the Postgraduate Certificate in Educationare a Graduate Entry Medicine studentELQ status impactA status of ELQ will not impact on the level of course fees you will be required to pay, but you will not be eligible for any financial support from Oxford or the UK government. If you did not complete your course, you might not receive funding for the full length of your studies at Oxford and should contact your funding agency to check your entitlement.Students undertaking the 6-year medicine degree are eligible to apply for a maintenance loan for living costs, even when they already hold a qualification that is equivalent or higher in level of study. Am I an ELQ student?You are an ELQ student if you study for a qualification of an equivalent or lower level to one you already hold. If you have studied for, but did not complete or were not awarded a qualification you should use your next highest qualification to do your calculations. If you hold an honorary degree (including the Oxbridge MA), this does not count as a relevant qualification when determining whether you are an ELQ student, you should use your other qualifications for your calculations. If you hold an MA from a Scottish institution where for historical reasons an MA is awarded instead of a BA and this is the highest qualification you hold, please use the Bachelor's degree group (Group 1) for your calculations. source.rawText: The Glasgow School of ArtThe Glasgow School of Art (GSA) is internationally recognised as one of Europe's top university-level institutions in the visual creative disciplines. It is ranked 3rd in the UK and 8th in the world for art and design in the QS World University Subject Rankings 2026. Based in the heart of Glasgow with connections across the globe, our studio-based teaching and world-leading research spans art, design, architecture, innovation and technology, making a significant difference to contemporary society.Learn More →Feed Install View, Communication Design, Degree Show 2026.What’s OnMaster of Fine Art Degree Show 2026 →Study at the GSA Studying at the GSA is an immersive creative experience, with studio-based programmes across our four specialist schools: Fine Art, Design, Architecture, and Innovation & Technology. Explore our degree programmes at undergraduate and postgraduate levels, as well as short courses, portfolio classes and exchange and study abroad options.Learn More →Undergraduate ProgrammesDuncan Brown, BA(Hons Fashion Design, 2025. Postgraduate Taught ProgrammesZiqi Chen, MLitt Contempoary Art Practice, 2025. Postgraduate Research ProgrammesAccommodationShowcasesDiscover bold, provocative and eclectic work by recent graduates on our Graduate Showcases: digital platforms collating individual presentations of graduate work alongside thematic interrogations.Learn More →Undergraduate ShowcaseAnna Coyle, Mackintosh School of Architecture, Stage 3, 2025. Postgraduate ShowcaseKirsten Farquhar, MDes Sound for the Moving Image, 2025. ResearchThe GSA is home to a vibrant community of research staff and students, with expertise spanning the disciplines of creative practice and theory. In REF 2021, 88% of the GSA's research impact was judged to be world-leading and internationally excellent, furthering the GSA’s position as one of the UK’s leading higher education institutions in art and design.
